# Appendix S1. Spatial analyses

Wolf and jackal covariates were detection-corrected relative site-level activity indices, not estimates of predator density. The archived manuscript specification used intercept-only predator state models and detection models containing path type, camera model, vegetation structure, and area behind the camera; empirical-Bayes site effects were extracted and standardized. The original predator-index fit objects and candidate-fit statistics were not retained, so this provenance is reported explicitly rather than reconstructed.

The joint negative-binomial `spAbundance::lfMsNMix` model used open-space cover and the wolf × jackal activity structure in the state process, effort and cattle activity in detection, and two latent factors. Open-space cover was specified a priori rather than selected by information-criterion comparison. The class-specific negative-binomial `NMix` models used wolf × jackal activity in the state process and the same detection covariates. Bayesian fits used three chains of 50,000 iterations, a 5,000-iteration burn-in, and thinning by 10; posterior predictive checks, R-hat, and effective sample size were used diagnostically. Class-specific priors were normal with variance 100 for state coefficients and 2.72 for detection coefficients, with a Uniform(0, 10) negative-binomial dispersion prior; the joint model used the corresponding community normal priors, inverse-gamma(0.1, 0.1) among-class variance priors, and class-specific Uniform(0, 10) dispersion priors. Conditional ratios were calculated draw by draw, and matched `unmarked::pcount` models provided a parallel-framework sensitivity analysis.

# Appendix S2. Juvenile:female ratio

Camera-round juvenile and adult-female counts were analyzed with a beta-binomial mixed model for 221 informative camera-rounds at 50 cameras. All six candidates retained open-space, built-and-road, nature-reserve, human-activity, and camera-design adjustments, plus camera nested within polygon random intercepts. Only predator and survey-period structure varied. The implemented Early period included camera-round midpoints on or before 17 October 2020 and Late included later midpoints; no midpoint fell exactly on the boundary. Candidate models were compared by AIC, and nested extensions were evaluated by likelihood-ratio tests.

# Appendix S3. Diel activity analyses

Apparent solar time was calculated from corrected UTC timestamps using longitude and the date-specific equation of time, preserving equal one-hour durations while aligning solar noon to 12:00. Astronomical night was solar elevation below 0°, and class-specific kernel overlap used the Dhat4 estimator. For the hierarchical analysis, each positive-effort camera-round contributed 24 one-hour binomial histories; zero-success hours were retained and recorded operational days supplied the trials. Cyclic binomial GAMs included survey round, camera and camera-round structure, and, where selected, camera-specific cyclic deviations.

Baseline, wolf-only, jackal-only, additive, and wolf × jackal temporal structures were compared by AIC, retaining the least-complex candidate within 2 AIC units of the minimum. Predicted curves were normalized within predator context and therefore represent redistribution across the 24-hour cycle. The seven-specification audit comprised the primary apparent-solar fit, k = 8, k = 16, sun time, an alternate camera-only hierarchy, independent 30-min histories, and sun time plus the camera-only hierarchy. The confirmatory joint GAM used common predator-time smooths and symmetric sum-to-zero demographic deviation smooths with penalty-aware boundary tests.
